boundToCoreContract: framework/registries/PAF-Technology-Registry.json (CORE ships with zero entries; the stack is Profile content)
approvalRule: An agent may use only entries listed ACTIVE here. An unlisted technology, tool, or dependency is DENIED by default (CR-5), regardless of convenience, familiarity, or apparent suitability. Adding an entry is a governed change.

versionPinningPolicy.rule: Minor versions are pinned here. EXACT PATCH VERSIONS ARE NOT ASSERTED IN THIS REGISTRY — they move monthly and must be captured at install time (Steps 87-100) into committed lockfiles.
versionPinningPolicy.reproducibilitySource: uv.lock (Python) and package-lock.json (frontend) are the authoritative reproducibility record. Both MUST be committed.
versionPinningPolicy.honestyNote: Version currency was verified against python.org on 2026-08-14 (Python 3.14.7 latest feature series, 3.13.15 latest maintenance). Other version ranges are minor-version floors based on known-current majors, not verified patch-by-patch. Re-verify at install time rather than trusting this record.

approvedEntries.name: Python
approvedEntries.role: Backend runtime
approvedEntries.notes: Python 3.13 selected over 3.14. 3.14 changed annotation evaluation semantics; 3.13 has a full maintenance year and the best wheel availability for pyodbc and numpy, which matter more here than new syntax. 3.13's experimental free-threaded (GIL-free) build mode is EXPLICITLY NOT RELIED UPON — library support is unreliable, and AC-MINING-PLACEMENT already removes the need for it by keeping computation in SQL.

alternativesRejected.reason: Annotation evaluation change plus less mature wheel coverage for critical libraries.

approvedEntries.name: Node.js
approvedEntries.role: Frontend build toolchain only — not an application runtime
approvedEntries.notes: Node 24 LTS. Amended from the initial >=22,<23 entry: Node 24 became LTS after that entry was written, and the owner's machine already had 24.16.0. The registry describes reality; downgrading a machine to match a document written from stale information is backwards. Node is used ONLY to build the React frontend — it never runs the application — so runtime risk is nil. Residual risk: some frontend tooling lags on new Node majors. This will be exercised at Step 102 when the build first runs; if it breaks, install nvm-windows and pin 22 THEN, with recorded evidence rather than as a precaution.

approvedEntries.name: Numbered forward-only SQL scripts (db-build-sop)
approvedEntries.role: Schema definition and deployment
approvedEntries.notes: DECISION B. A migration framework was deliberately REJECTED. Alembic exists to make schema churn frictionless — autogenerate a diff, apply it. DDR P-8 says structural migration against populated tenant data is the thing to avoid. A tool that makes migrations easy works against a principle that says do not need them. Numbered forward-only scripts under the existing db-build-sop (run_all / teardown / manifest / verify) keep DDL reviewable as SQL, which matters when the DDL IS the design.

alternativesRejected.reason: Optimises for frequent schema change, which is the opposite of the P-8 no-migration posture. Autogenerated diffs also reduce DDL reviewability.

approvedEntries.name: uv
approvedEntries.role: Python dependency and virtual environment management, plus Python version pinning
approvedEntries.notes: DECISION C. Selected over pip-tools. Reasoning corrected during discussion: pip + requirements.txt is NOT reproducible, so a locking tool was mandatory and the real choice was WHICH lock tool. uv is FEWER concepts than pip-tools (one command vs a .in file, a compile step and a .txt file), which matters for an owner learning either tool for the first time. uv also installs and pins the Python interpreter, removing a separate moving part on Windows.

alternativesRejected.reason: Not reproducible — fails Step 83's completion criterion outright.
Mature and community-maintained, but slower and MORE concepts to learn. Remains the documented fallback.
Wants to own project layout and packaging; unnecessary for an application rather than a library.

approvedEntries.name: Pydantic
approvedEntries.role: Runtime data validation at trust boundaries
approvedEntries.notes:
Added on owner query. NEEDED, not optional: FastAPI uses Pydantic for request/response validation, so it arrives with the approved backend framework regardless. Distinct from mypy — mypy checks types at author time, Pydantic validates data at runtime. Both are used; they cooperate, and mypy understands Pydantic models.

PRIMARY PROJECT ROLE: enforce the event log data contract (504) at the ingestion boundary. Malformed client submissions are rejected with a specific, reportable error rather than admitted and discovered later — supports the fail-visibly posture and D-31/US-FA23-4 client-facing validation traceability.

PLACEMENT CONSTRAINT: Pydantic validates at trust boundaries (API request bodies, ingestion input, configuration loading). It MUST NOT be used to validate row-by-row over event data in Python — that would violate AC-MINING-PLACEMENT. Bulk data-quality checks belong in SQL against the loaded set; Pydantic guards the door, not the warehouse floor.
